When the Box marks their last HP, the magic powering them ruptures in an explosion of force. All targets within Close range must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or take 2d8+1 magic damage.
A cube-shaped construct with a different rune on each of their six sides.
system.motives: Change tactics, trample foes, wait in disguise

system.description: The Skull levitates several feet off the ground and can’t be Restrained.
The Skull is resistant to magic damage.
Mark a Stress to make an attack against all targets within Close range. Targets the Skull succeeds against take 2d6+4 magic damage.

Spend a Fear to make an attack against a PC with a Spellcast trait within Very Close range. On a success, the target marks 1d4 Stress and the Skull clears that many Stress. Additionally, on a success, the Skull can immediately be spotlighted again.
A floating humanoid skull animated by scintillating magic.
system.motives: Cackle, consume magic, serve creator

system.description: The Conscript is defeated when they take any damage. For every 6 damage a PC deals to the Conscript, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Conscripts within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 6 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
A poorly trained civilian pressed into war.
system.motives: Follow orders, gang up, survive

system.description: When a PC within Close range makes a Presence Roll, you can mark a Stress to cast a gaze toward the aftermath. On the target’s failure, they must mark 2 Stress and are Vulnerable until the scene ends or they succeed on a social action against the Courtesan. On the target’s success, they must mark a Stress.
An accomplished manipulator and master of the social arts.
system.motives: Entice, maneuver, secure patrons

system.description: Spend a Fear to make a standard attack against a target within range. On a success, the target must mark a Stress.
Mark a Stress to wrap an ally within Close range in a shroud of Protection until the Adept marks their last HP. While Protected, the target has resistance to all damage.

Spend a Fear and choose a point within Far range. All targets within Close range of that point are Restrained in smoky chains until they break free with a successful Strength or Instinct Roll. A target Restrained by this feature must spend a Hope to make an action roll.
Twice per scene, when a PC rolls a failure with Fear, clear a Stress.
An experienced mage wielding shadow and fear.
system.motives: Curry favor, hinder foes, uncover knowledge

system.description: The Fang can climb and walk on vertical surfaces. Mark a Stress to move from one shadow to another within Far range.

Mark a Stress to cause a target within Melee range to make an Instinct Reaction Roll. On a failure, the target must mark 2 Stress and is teleported with the Fang to a shadow within Far range, making them temporarily Vulnerable. On a success, the target must mark a Stress.
A professional killer-turned-cultist.
system.motives: Capture sacrifices, isolate prey, rise in the ranks

system.description: The Initiate is defeated when they take any damage. For every 6 damage a PC deals to the Initiate, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Cult Initiates within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 5 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
A low-ranking cultist in simple robes, eager to gain power.
system.motives: Follow orders, gain power, seek forbidden knowledge

system.description: When the Pack has marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals 2d4+1 physical damage instead.
Mark a Stress to make all targets within Very Close range lose a Hope. If a target is not able to lose a Hope, they must instead mark 2 Stress.
When the Pack makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
Unnatural hounds lit from within by hellfire.
system.motives: Cause fear, consume flesh, please masters

system.description: When the Eels have marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals 2d4+1 physical damage instead.
Mark a Stress to make a standard attack against all targets within Very Close range. You gain a Fear for each target that marks HP.
A swarm of eels that encircle and electrocute.
system.motives: Avoid larger predators, shock prey, tear apart

system.description: Mark a Stress to move into Melee range of an ally and make a standard attack against a target within Very Close range. On a success, deal 2d10+2 physical damage and the ally can clear a Stress.
When the Soldier is within Very Close range of a knight or other noble who would take damage, you can mark a Stress to move into Melee range of them and take the damage instead.
An armored squire or experienced commoner looking to advance.
system.motives: Gain glory, keep order, make alliances

system.description: The Experiment is resistant to physical damage.
When a target the Experiment attacks has other adversaries within Very Close range, the Experiment deals double damage.
Mark a Stress to spotlight the Experiment as an additional GM move instead of spending Fear.
A magical necromantic experiment gone wrong, leaving them warped and ungainly.
system.motives: Devour, hunt, track

system.description: When the Beastmaster is spotlighted, you can also spotlight a Tier 1 animal adversary currently under their control.

Make a standard attack against a target. On a success, you can mark a Stress to pin them to a nearby surface. The pinned target is Restrained until they break free with a successful Finesse or Strength Roll.
Twice per scene, summon a Bear, Dire Wolf, or similar Tier 1 animal adversary under the Beastmaster’s control. The adversary appears at Close range and is immediately spotlighted.
A leather-clad warrior bearing a whip and massive bow.
system.motives: Command, make a living, maneuver, pin down, protect companion animals

system.description: Mark a Stress to have the Brawler charge at an inanimate object within Close range they could feasibly smash (such as a wall, cart, or market stand) and destroy it. All targets within Very Close range of the object must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 2d4+3 physical damage from the shrapnel.

When the Brawler marks 2 or more HP from an attack within Very Close range, you can make a standard attack against the attacker. On a success, the Brawler deals 2d6+15 physical damage instead of their standard damage.
When the Brawler makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
An especially muscular giant wielding a warhammer larger than a human.
system.motives: Make a living, overwhelm, slam, topple

system.description: The Recruit is defeated when they take any damage. For every 7 damage a PC deals to the Recruit, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Giant Recruits within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 5 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
A giant fighter wearing borrowed armor.
system.motives: Batter, make a living, overwhelm, terrify

system.description: While flying, the Eagle gains a +3 bonus to their Difficulty.
Mark a Stress to attack a target within Far range. On a success, deal 2d10+2 physical damage and knock the target over, making them Vulnerable until they next act.

Make an attack against a target within Very Close range. On a success, deal 2d4+3 physical damage and the target must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or become temporarily Restrained within the Eagle’s massive talons. If the target is Restrained, the Eagle immediately lifts into the air to Very Far range above the battlefield while holding them.

While flying, the Eagle can drop a Restrained target they are holding. When dropped, the target is no longer Restrained but starts falling. If their fall isn’t prevented during the PCs’ next action, the target takes 2d20 physical damage when they land.
A giant bird of prey with blood-stained talons.
system.motives: Hunt prey, stay mobile, strike decisively

system.description: The Gorgon can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
When the Gorgon makes a successful standard attack, the target Glows until the end of the scene and can’t become Hidden. Attack rolls made against a Glowing target have advantage.
Make an attack roll against a target within Melee range using the Gorgon’s protective snakes. On a success, mark a Stress to deal 2d10+4 physical damage and the target must mark a Stress.

When the Gorgon takes damage from an attack within Close range, you can spend a Fear to force the attacker to make an Instinct Reaction Roll. On a failure, they begin to turn to stone, marking a HP and starting a Petrification Countdown (4). This countdown ticks down when the Gorgon is attacked. When it triggers, the target must make a death move. If the Gorgon is defeated, all petrification countdowns end.
When the Gorgon makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
A snake-headed, scaled humanoid with a gilded bow, enraged that their peace has been disturbed.
system.motives: Corner, hit-and-run, petrify, seek vengeance

system.description: The Flickerfly can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
Before the Flickerfly makes an attack, roll a d6. On a result of 4 or higher, the target’s Evasion is halved against this attack.

Mark a Stress to create a magically dazzling display that grapples the minds of nearby foes. All targets within Close range must make an Instinct Reaction Roll. For each target who failed, you gain a Fear and the Flickerfly learns one of the target’s fears.

Countdown (Loop 1d6). When the Flickerfly takes damage for the first time, activate the countdown. When it triggers, the Flickerfly breathes hallucinatory gas on all targets in front of them up to Far range. Targets must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be tormented by fearful hallucinations. Targets whose fears are known to the Flickerfly have disadvantage on this roll. Targets who fail must mark a Stress and lose a Hope.
A horse-sized insect with iridescent scales and crystalline wings moving faster than the eye can see.
system.motives: Collect shiny things, hunt, swoop

system.description: While the Knight is on a mount, they gain a +2 bonus to their Difficulty. When they take Severe damage, they’re knocked from their mount and lose this benefit until they’re next spotlighted.
When the Knight takes physical damage, reduce it by 3.
If the Knight is mounted, move up to Far range and make a standard attack against a target. On a success, deal 2d8+4 physical damage and the target must mark a Stress.
Mark a Stress to spotlight 1d4+1 allies. Attacks they make while spotlighted in this way deal half damage.
A decorated soldier with heavy armor and a powerful steed.
system.motives: Run down, seek glory, show dominance

system.description: Make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d8+2 physical damage and the Thief steals one item or consumable from the target’s inventory.

Mark a Stress to reveal a snare trap set anywhere on the battlefield by the Thief. All targets within Very Close range of the trap must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (13) or be pulled off their feet and suspended upside down. A target is Restrained and Vulnerable until they break free, ending both conditions, with a successful Finesse or Strength Roll (13).
A cunning thief with acrobatic skill and a flair for the dramatic.
system.motives: Evade, hide, pilfer, profit

system.description: Spend a Fear to offer a target a dangerous bargain for something they want or need. If used on a PC, they must make a Presence Reaction Roll (17). On a failure, they must mark 2 Stress or take the deal.

items.name: The Best Muscle Money Can Buy

system.description: Once per scene, mark a Stress to summon 1d4+1 Tier 1 adversaries, who appear at Far range, to enforce the Baron’s will.
An accomplished merchant with a large operation under their command.
system.motives: Abuse power, gather resources, mobilize minions

system.description: You must spend a Fear to spotlight the Minotaur. While spotlighted, they can make their standard attack against all targets within range.

Mark a Stress to charge through a group within Close range and make an attack against all targets in the Minotaur’s path. Targets the Minotaur succeeds against take 2d6+8 physical damage and are knocked back to Very Far range. If a target is knocked into a solid object or another creature, they take an extra 1d6 damage (combine the damage).
Make an attack against a target within Very Close range, moving the Minotaur into Melee range of them. On a success, deal 2d8 direct physical damage.
A massive bull-headed firbolg with a quick temper.
system.motives: Consume, gore, navigate, overpower, pursue

system.description: When the Hunter makes a successful attack, all PCs within Far range lose a Hope and you gain a Fear.

Spend a Fear to curse a target within Very Close range with a necrotic Deathlock until the end of the scene. Attacks made by the Hunter against a Deathlocked target deal direct damage. The Hunter can only maintain one Deathlock at a time.
Mark a Stress to spotlight 1d4 allies. Attacks they make while spotlighted in this way deal half damage.

Countdown (Loop 1d6). When the Hunter is in the spotlight for the first time, activate the countdown. When it triggers, move the Hunter in a straight line to a point within Far range and make an attack against all targets in their path. Targets the Hunter succeeds against take 2d8+2 physical damage.
An undead figure wearing a heavy leather coat, with searching eyes and a casually cruel demeanor.
system.motives: Devour, hunt, track

system.description: A PC who rolls less than 17 on an action roll targeting the Advisor must mark a Stress.

Mark a Stress to influence an NPC within Melee range with whispered words. That target’s opinion on one matter shifts toward the Advisor’s preference unless it is in direct opposition to the target’s motives.

Spend a Fear to convince a crowd or notable individual that one person or group is responsible for some problem facing the target. The target becomes hostile to the scapegoat until convinced of their innocence with a successful Presence Roll (17).
A high-ranking courtier with the ear of the local nobility.
system.motives: Curry favor, manufacture evidence, scheme

system.description: Spend 2 Fear to spotlight 1d4 allies. Attacks they make while spotlighted in this way deal half damage.
When you spotlight an ally within Far range, mark a Stress to gain a Fear.

Countdown (6). When the Secret-Keeper is in the spotlight for the first time, activate the countdown. When they mark HP, tick down this countdown by the number of HP marked. When it triggers, summon a Minor Demon who appears at Close range.
Once per scene, when the SecretKeeper marks 2 or more HP, you can mark a Stress to summon a Demonic Hound Pack, which appears at Close range and is immediately spotlighted.
A clandestine leader with a direct channel to the Fallen Gods.
system.motives: Amass great power, plot, take command

system.description: When the Shark makes a successful attack, all PCs within Far range lose a Hope and you gain a Fear.

When the Shark makes a successful attack, the target must mark an Armor Slot without receiving its benefits (they can still use armor to reduce the damage). If they can’t mark an Armor Slot, they must mark an additional HP.

When a creature within Close range of the Shark marks HP from another creature’s attack, you can mark a Stress to immediately spotlight the Shark, moving them into Melee range of the target and making a standard attack.
A large aquatic predator, always on the move.
system.motives: Find the blood, isolate prey, target the weak

system.description: If the Siren makes a standard attack against a target Entranced by their song, the attack deals 2d10+1 damage instead of their standard damage.

Spend a Fear to sing a song that affects all targets within Close range. Targets must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or become Entranced until they mark 2 Stress. Other Sirens within Close range of the target can mark a Stress to each add a +1 bonus to the Difficulty of the reaction roll. While Entranced, a target can’t act and is Vulnerable.
A half-fish person with shimmering scales and an irresistible voice.
system.motives: Consume, lure prey, subdue with song

system.description: The Archer has resistance to physical damage. Mark a Stress to move up to Close range through solid objects.
Spend a Fear to make an attack within Far range against a PC who is within Very Close range of at least two other PCs. On a success, the target takes 2d8+12 physical damage.
A ghostly fighter with an ethereal bow, unable to move on while their charge is vulnerable.
system.motives: Move through solid objects, stay out of the fray, rehash old battles

system.description: The Captain has resistance to physical damage. Mark a Stress to move up to Close range through solid objects.
Spend 2 Fear to return up to 1d4+1 defeated Spectral allies to the battle at the points where they first appeared (with no marked HP or Stress).
When the Captain’s Spectral allies are forced to make a reaction roll, you can mark a Stress to give those allies a +2 bonus to the roll.
When the Captain makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
A ghostly commander leading their troops beyond death.
system.motives: Move through solid objects, rally troops, rehash old battles

system.description: The Guardian has resistance to physical damage. Mark a Stress to move up to Close range through solid objects.
Spend a Fear to make an attack against a target within Very Close range. On a success, deal 2d10+6 physical damage and the target must mark a Stress.
A ghostly fighter with spears and swords, anchored by duty.
system.motives: Move through solid objects, protect treasure, rehash old battles

system.description: Spend a Fear to describe how the Spy knows a secret about a PC in the scene.

When a PC or group is discussing something sensitive, you can mark a Stress to reveal that the Spy is present in the scene, observing them. If the Spy escapes the scene to report their findings, you gain 1d4 Fear.
A skilled espionage agent with a knack for being in the right place to overhear secrets.
system.motives: Cut and run, disguise appearance, eavesdrop

system.description: The Stonewraith can move through stone and earth as easily as air. While within stone or earth, they are Hidden and immune to all damage.

While Hidden, mark a Stress to leap into Melee range with a target within Very Close range. The target must succeed on an Agility or Instinct Reaction Roll (15) or take 2d8 physical damage and become temporarily Restrained.

Spend a Fear to roar while within a cave and cause a cave-in. All targets within Close range must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll (14) or take 2d10 physical damage. The rubble can be cleared with a Progress Countdown (8).
When the Stonewraith makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
A prowling hunter, like a slinking mountain lion, with a slate-gray stone body.
system.motives: Defend territory, isolate prey, stalk

system.description: Before or after making a standard attack, you can mark a Stress to teleport to a location within Far range.
Mark a Stress to refresh the Wizard’s “Warding Sphere” reaction.

Spend a Fear and choose a point within Far range. A Very Close area around that point erupts into impassable terrain. All targets within that area must make an Agility Reaction Roll (14). Targets who fail take 2d10 physical damage and are thrown out of the area. Targets who succeed take half damage and aren’t moved.
Spend a Fear to unleash a precise hail of magical blasts. All targets in the scene must make an Agility Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 2d12 magic damage. Targets who succeed take half damage.

When the Wizard takes damage from an attack within Close range, deal 2d6 magic damage to the attacker. This reaction can’t be used again until the Wizard refreshes it with their “Refresh Warding Sphere” action.
A battle-hardened mage trained in destructive magic.
system.motives: Develop new spells, seek power, shatter formations

system.description: The Flickerfly can be spotlighted up to four times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
When the Flickerfly makes an attack, the target’s Evasion is halved against the attack.
While flying, the Flickerfly can move up to Far range instead of Close range before taking an action.
Spend a Fear to whirl, making an attack against all targets within Very Close range. Targets the Flickerfly succeeds against take 3d8 direct physical damage.

Mark a Stress to create a magically dazzling display that grapples the minds of nearby foes. All targets within Close range must make an Instinct Reaction Roll. For each target who failed, you gain a Fear and the Flickerfly learns one of the target’s fears.

Countdown (Loop 1d6). When the Flickerfly takes damage for the first time, activate the countdown. When it triggers, the Flickerfly breathes hallucinatory gas on all targets in front of them up to Far range. Targets must make an Instinct Reaction Roll or be tormented by fearful hallucinations. Targets whose fears are known to the Flickerfly have disadvantage on this roll. Targets who fail lose 2 Hope and take 3d8+3 direct magic damage.
When the Flickerfly takes damage from an attack within Close range, you can mark a Stress to take half damage.
A winged insect the size of a large house with iridescent scales and wings that move too fast to track.
system.motives: Collect shiny things, hunt, nest, swoop

system.description: Attacks against the Demon are made with disadvantage unless the attacker spends a handful of gold. This Demon starts with a number of handfuls equal to the number of PCs. When a target marks HP from the Demon’s standard attack, they can spend a handful of gold instead of marking HP (1 handful per HP). Add a handful of gold to the Demon for each handful of gold spent by PCs on this feature.
Add a bonus to the Demon’s attack rolls equal to the number of handfuls of gold they have.
Spend 3 handfuls of gold (or a Fear) to spotlight 1d4+1 allies.
A regal cloaked monstrosity with circular horns adorned with treasure.
system.motives: Consume, fuel greed, sow dissent

system.description: The Demon deals double damage to PCs with 0 Hope.
Spend a Fear to weigh down the spirits of all PCs within Far range. All targets affected replace their Hope Die with a d8 until they roll a success with Hope or their next rest.
When a PC fails with Fear, you can mark a Stress to cause all other PCs within Close range to lose a Hope.
When the Demon makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
A cloaked demon-creature with long limbs, seeping shadows.
system.motives: Make fear contagious, stick to the shadows, undermine resolve

system.description: When the Demon makes a successful attack, all PCs within Far range must lose a Hope and you gain a Fear.
When a PC within Far range fails a roll, they can choose to reroll their Fear Die and take the new result. If they still fail, they mark 2 Stress and the Demon clears a Stress.
Mark a Stress to deal the Demon’s standard attack damage to a target within Close range.
Spend a Fear to spotlight two other Demons within Far range.
When a PC fails a roll within Close range of the Demon, they must mark a Stress.
A perfectly beautiful and infinitely cruel demon with a gleaming spear and elegant robes.
system.motives: Condescend, declare premature victory, prove superiority

system.description: The Demon’s attacks deal direct damage.
Spend a Fear to boil the blood of all PCs within Far range. They use a d20 as their Fear Die until the end of the scene.
When the Demon takes damage from an attack within Close range, you can mark a Stress to make a standard attack against the attacker.

Countdown (Loop 6). Activate the first time an attack is made within sight of the Demon. It ticks down when a PC takes a violent action. When it triggers, summon 1d4 Minor Demons, who appear at Close range.
A hulking demon with boulder-sized fists, driven by endless rage.
system.motives: Fuel anger, impress rivals, wreak havoc

system.description: The Demon’s standard attack deals direct damage.
When the Demon marks HP from an attack, spend a number of Fear equal to the HP marked by the Demon to cause the attacker to mark the same number of HP.
When a creature within Close range takes damage from a different adversary, you can mark a Stress to add a d4 to the damage roll.

When a PC takes Severe damage within Very Close range of the Demon, you can spend a Fear to cause the target to make a Finesse Reaction Roll. On a failure, the Demon seizes one item or consumable of their choice from the target’s inventory.
A fickle creature of spindly limbs and insatiable desires.
system.motives: Join in on others’ success, take what belongs to others, hold grudges

system.description: While flying, the Bat gains a +3 bonus to their Difficulty.
Mark a Stress to send a high-pitch screech out toward all targets in front of the Bat within Far range. Those targets must mark 1d4 Stress.
When an allied Vampire marks HP, you can mark a Stress to fly into Melee range of the attacker and make an attack with advantage against them. On a success, deal 2d6+2 physical damage.
A wide-winged pet endlessly loyal to their vampire owner.
system.motives: Dive-bomb, hide, protect leader

system.description: Mark a Stress to target a point within Far range. Create a patch of thorns that covers an area within Close range of that point. All targets within that area take 2d6+2 physical damage when they act. A target must succeed on a Finesse Roll or deal more than 20 damage to the Dryad with an attack to leave the area.
Spend a Fear to grow three Treant Sapling Minions, who appear at Close range and immediately take the spotlight.
When an ally dies within Close range, you can spend a Fear to clear 2 HP and 2 Stress as the fallen ally’s life force is returned to the forest.
A nature spirit in the form of a humanoid tree.
system.motives: Command, cultivate, drive out, preserve the forest

system.description: The Elemental is defeated when they take any damage. For every 9 damage a PC deals to the Elemental, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Elemental Sparks within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 5 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
A blazing mote of elemental fire.
system.motives: Blast, consume, gain mass

system.description: When you spotlight the Elemental and they don’t have a token on their stat block, they can’t act yet. Place a token on their stat block and describe what they’re preparing to do. When you spotlight the Elemental and they have a token on their stat block, clear the token and they can act.

When the Elemental makes a successful attack, the target must mark an Armor Slot without receiving its benefits (they can still use armor to reduce the damage). If they can’t mark an Armor Slot, they must mark an additional HP.
An attack that would move the Elemental moves them two fewer ranges (for example, Far becomes Very Close). When the Elemental takes physical damage, reduce it by 7.

Mark a Stress to create a rockslide that buries the land in front of Elemental within Close range with rockfall. All targets in this area must make an Agility Reaction Roll (19). Targets who fail take 2d12+5 physical damage and become Vulnerable until their next roll with Hope. Targets who succeed take half damage.
When the Elemental makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
A living landslide of boulders and dust, as large as a house.
system.motives: Avalanche, knock over, pummel

system.description: Mark a Stress to attack a target within Very Close range. On a success, deal 2d4+7 physical damage and the target’s next action has disadvantage. On a failure, the target must mark a Stress.

Spend a Fear to make an attack against all targets within Very Close range. Targets the Elemental succeeds against become Restrained and Vulnerable as they begin drowning. A target can break free, ending both conditions, with a successful Strength or Instinct Roll.
When the Elemental makes a successful standard attack, you can mark a Stress to knock the target back to Close range.
A huge living wave that crashes down upon enemies.
system.motives: Deluge, disperse, drown

system.description: When you spotlight the Ooze and they don’t have a token on their stat block, they can’t act yet. Place a token on their stat block and describe what they’re preparing to do. When you spotlight the Ooze and they have a token on their stat block, clear the token and they can act.

When the Ooze makes a successful attack, the target must mark an Armor Slot without receiving its benefits (they can still use armor to reduce the damage). If they can’t mark an Armor Slot, they must mark an additional HP.

Make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, the Ooze Envelops them and the target must mark 2 Stress. While Enveloped, the target must mark an additional Stress every time they make an action roll. When the Ooze takes Severe damage, all Enveloped targets are freed and the condition is cleared.
When the Ooze has 4 or more HP marked, you can spend a Fear to split them into two Green Oozes (with no marked HP or Stress). Immediately spotlight both of them.
A translucent green mound of acid taller than most humans.
system.motives: Camouflage, creep up, envelop, multiply

system.description: The Hydra begins with three heads and can have up to five. When the Hydra takes Major or greater damage, they lose a head.
The Hydra can be spotlighted X times per GM turn, where X is the Hydra’s number of heads. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
If the Hydra has any marked HP, spend a Fear to clear a HP and grow two heads.
All PCs within Far range lose 2 Hope.
When the Hydra takes magic damage, they become Dazed until the next roll with Fear. While Dazed, they can’t use their Regeneration action but are immune to magic damage.
A quadrupedal scaled beast with multiple long-necked heads, each filled with menacing fangs.
system.motives: Devour, regenerate, terrify

system.description: Spend a Fear per PC in the party to have the group condemned for crimes real or imagined. A PC who succeeds on a Presence Roll can demand trial by combat or another special form of trial.
Once per scene, mark a Stress to summon six Tier 3 Minions, who appear at Close range to enforce the Monarch’s will.

Long-Term Countdown (8). Spend a Fear to activate after the Monarch’s desire for war is first revealed. When it triggers, the Monarch has a reason to rally the nation to war and the support to act on that reason. You gain 1d4 Fear.
The sovereign ruler of a nation, wreathed in the privilege of tradition and wielding unmatched power in their domain.
system.motives: Control vassals, destroy rivals, forge a legacy

system.description: When the Knight succeeds on a standard attack from above a target, they deal 3d12+3 physical damage instead of their standard damage.
Spend a Fear to make an attack against all targets within Very Close range. Targets the Knight succeeds against take physical damage equal to 3d4 + the target’s Major threshold.
When the Knight takes damage from an attack within Melee range, you can mark a Stress to deal 1d10+5 physical damage to the attacker.
A knight with huge, majestic antlers wearing armor made of dangerous thorns.
system.motives: Isolate, maneuver, protect the forest, weed the unwelcome

system.description: Before they make their first attack in a fight or after they become Hidden, the Treant is indistinguishable from other trees until they next act or a PC succeeds on an Instinct Roll to identify them.
Mark a Stress and make an attack against up to three targets within Close range, pummeling them with giant acorns. Targets the Treant succeeds against take 2d10+5 physical damage.

Mark a Stress to Root the Treant in place. The Treant is Restrained while Rooted, and can end this effect instead of moving while they are spotlighted. While Rooted, the Treant has resistance to physical damage.
A sturdy animate old-growth tree.
system.motives: Hide in plain sight, preserve the forest, root down, swing branches

system.description: The Sapling is defeated when they take any damage. For every 6 damage a PC deals to the Sapling, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Treant Saplings within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 8 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
A small, sentient tree sapling.
system.motives: Blend in, preserve the forest, pummel, surround

system.description: When the Vampire makes a successful attack, all PCs within Far range lose a Hope and you gain a Fear.
A creature who moves into Melee range of the Vampire must make an Instinct Reaction Roll. On a failure, you gain 1d4 Fear.
When the Vampire is within Melee range of an ally, they can cause the ally to mark a HP. The Vampire then clears a HP.
Spend 2 Fear to summon 1d4 Vampires, who appear at Far range and immediately take the spotlight.
When the Vampire is spotlighted, roll a d8. On a result of 6 or higher, all targets within Very Close range must mark a HP.
A captivating undead dressed in aristocratic finery.
system.motives: Create thralls, charm, command, fly, intimidate

system.description: Make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 5d4 physical damage. A target who marks HP from this attack loses a Hope and must mark a Stress. The Vampire then clears a HP.
When the Vampire takes physical damage, you can spend a Fear to take half damage.
An intelligent undead with blood-stained lips and a predator’s smile.
system.motives: Bite, charm, deceive, feed, intimidate

system.description: Creatures within Melee range of the Gaoler have disadvantage on attack rolls against them. Creatures trapped inside the Gaoler are immune to this feature.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Very Close range. On a success, the target is Restrained within the Gaoler until freed with a successful Strength Roll (18). While Restrained, the target can only attack the Gaoler.
A boxy, dust-covered construct with thick metallic swinging doors on their torso.
system.motives: Carry away, entrap, protect, pummel

system.description: Targets who take damage from the Sentinel’s standard attack are knocked back to Very Close range.

Mark a Stress to choose a target within Very Close range to focus on. That target has disadvantage on attack rolls when they’re within Very Close range of the Sentinel. The Sentinel can only focus on one target at a time.

Spend a Fear to lob explosive magic at a point within Far range. All targets within Very Close range of that point must make an Agility Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 2d8+20 magic damage and are knocked back to Close range. Targets who succeed take half damage and aren’t knocked back.
When the Sentinel makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
A dust-covered golden construct with boxy limbs and a huge mace for a hand.
system.motives: Destroy at any cost, expunge, protect

system.description: When you spotlight the Turret and they don’t have a token on their stat block, they can’t make a standard attack. Place a token on their stat block and describe what they’re preparing to do. When you spotlight the Turret and they have a token on their stat block, clear the token and they can attack.
Spend a Fear to Mark a target within Far range until the Turret is destroyed or the Marked target becomes Hidden. While the target is Marked, their Evasion is halved.
When another adversary deals damage to a target within Far range of the Turret, you can mark a Stress to add the Turret’s standard attack damage to the damage roll.
When the Turret is destroyed, they explode. All targets within Close range must make an Agility Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 3d20 physical damage. Targets who succeed take half damage.
A massive living turret with reinforced armor and twelve pistondriven mechanical legs.
system.motives: Concentrate fire, lock down, mark, protect

system.description: The Dragon can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
If a target damaged by the Dragon doesn’t mark an Armor Slot to reduce the damage, they must mark a Stress.
When a PC rolls with Fear while within Far range of the Dragon, they lose a Hope.

Spend 2 Fear to release an icy whorl in front of the Dragon within Close range. All targets in this area must make an Agility Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 4d6+5 magic damage and are Restrained by ice until they break free with a successful Strength Roll. Targets who succeed must mark 2 Stress or take half damage.

Spend a Fear to have the Dragon unleash a huge downfall of snow and ice, covering all other creatures within Far range. All targets within this area must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be buried in snow and rocks, becoming Vulnerable until they dig themselves out from the debris. For each PC that fails the reaction roll, you gain a Fear.

When a creature makes a successful attack against the Dragon from within Very Close range, they must mark a Stress and become Chilled until their next rest or they clear a Stress. While they are Chilled, they have disadvantage on attack rolls.
When the Dragon makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
A glacier-blue dragon with four powerful limbs and frost-tinged wings.
system.motives: Avalanche, defend lair, fly, freeze, defend what is mine, maul

system.description: Mark a Stress to spotlight 1d4 allies. Attacks they make while spotlighted in this way deal half damage, or full damage if you spend a Fear.

Mark 2 Stress to cause all targets within Far range to make a Strength Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 2d20+12 magic damage and you gain a Fear. Targets who succeed take half damage. A target who marks 2 or more HP must also mark 2 Stress and becomes Vulnerable until they roll with Hope.
Spend a Fear to summon a Zombie Legion, which appears at Close range and immediately takes the spotlight.

When the Necromancer has marked 7 or more of their HP, you can spend a Fear to have them teleport away to a safe location to recover. A PC who succeeds on an Instinct Roll can trace the teleportation magic to their destination.

Countdown (Loop 2d6). When the Necromancer has marked 6 or more of their HP, activate the countdown. When it triggers, deal 2d10+6 direct magic damage to a target within Close range. The Necromancer then clears a number of Stress or HP equal to the number of HP marked by the target from this attack.
A decaying mage adorned in dark, tattered robes.
system.motives: Corrupt, decay, flee to fight another day, resurrect

system.description: Spend a Fear to unleash an all-consuming firestorm and make an attack against all targets within Close range. Targets the Sorcerer succeeds against take 2d10+6 direct magic damage.

Mark a Stress to trap a target within Far range in a powerful illusion of their worst fears. While trapped, the target is Restrained and Vulnerable until they break free, ending both conditions, with a successful Instinct Roll.
When the Sorcerer takes damage from an attack, they can teleport up to Far range.

Countdown (Loop 2d6). When the Sorcerer is in the spotlight for the first time, activate the countdown. When it triggers, all targets within Far range become Vulnerable and must mark a Stress as they relive their greatest regrets. A target can break free from their regret with a successful Presence or Strength Roll. When a PC fails to break free, they lose a Hope.
A powerful mage bound by the bargains they made in life.
system.motives: Acquire, dishearten, dominate, torment

system.description: The Shock Troop is defeated when they take any damage. For every 12 damage a PC deals to the Shock Troop, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.
When a PC marks HP from an attack by the Shock Troop, they lose a Hope.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Fallen Shock Troops within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 12 physical damage each. Combine this damage.

FALLEN WARLORD: realm-breaker

FALLEN WARLORD: undefeated champion
A cursed soul bound to the Fallen’s will.
system.motives: Crush, dominate, earn relief, punish

system.description: The Realm-Breaker can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
When the Realm-Breaker takes damage, reduce it by 2d10.
Mark a Stress to make a standard attack against all targets within Very Close range. When a target uses armor to reduce damage from this attack, they must mark 2 Armor Slots.

Countdown (Decreasing 8). When the Realm-Breaker is in the spotlight for the first time, activate the countdown. When it triggers, create a torrent of incarnate rage that rends flesh from bone. All targets within Far range must make a Presence Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 2d6+10 direct magic damage. Targets who succeed take half damage. For each HP marked from this damage, summon a Fallen Shock Troop within Very Close range of the target who marked that HP. If the countdown ever decreases its maximum value to 0, the Realm-Breaker marks their remaining HP and all targets within Far range must mark all remaining HP and make a death move.
When a target marks HP from an attack by the Realm-Breaker, all PCs within Far range of the target must lose a Hope.

items.name: I Have Never Known Defeat (Phase Change)

system.description: When the Realm-Breaker marks their last HP, replace them with the Undefeated Champion and immediately spotlight them.
A Fallen God, wreathed in rage and resentment, bearing millennia of experience in breaking heroes’ spirits.
system.motives: Corrupt, dominate, punish, break the weak

system.description: The Undefeated Champion can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
When the Undefeated Champion takes damage, reduce it by 1d10.
Mark a Stress to make a standard attack against all targets within Very Close range. PCs the Champion succeeds against lose a number of Hope equal to the HP they marked from this attack.
Spend a Fear to summon a number of Fallen Shock Troops equal to twice the number of PCs. The Shock Troops appear at Far range.

Countdown (1d8). When the Undefeated Champion is in the spotlight for the first time, activate the countdown. When it triggers, activate a magical circle covering an area within Far range of the Champion. A target within that area is Vulnerable until they leave the circle. The circle can be removed by dealing Severe damage to the Undefeated Champion.
When the Undefeated Champion makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
When a target marks HP from an attack by the Undefeated Champion, all PCs within Far range of the target lose a Hope.
That which only the most feared have a chance to fear.
system.motives: Dispatch merciless death, punish the defiant, secure victory at any cost

system.description: The Archer deals double damage to targets marked Guilty by a High Seraph.
Mark a Stress to make a standard attack against up to three targets.
Spirit soldiers with sanctified bows.
system.motives: Focus fire, obey, reposition, volley

system.description: The Soldier is defeated when they take any damage. For every 13 damage a PC deals to the Soldier, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.
While the Soldier is flying, spend a Fear to move up to Far range instead of Close range before taking an action.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Hallowed Soldiers within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 10 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
Souls of the faithful, lifted up with divine weaponry.
system.motives: Obey, outmaneuver, punish, swarm

system.description: The Seraph can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
While the Seraph is flying, spend a Fear to move up to Far range instead of Close range before taking an action.

Spend a Fear to make a target Guilty in the eyes of the Seraph’s god until the Seraph is defeated. While Guilty, the target doesn’t gain Hope on a result with Hope. When the Seraph succeeds on a standard attack against a Guilty target, they deal Severe damage instead of their standard damage. The Seraph can only mark one target at a time.

Mark a Stress to reflect a sliver of divinity as a searing beam of light that hits up to twenty targets within Very Far range. Targets must make a Presence Reaction Roll, with disadvantage if they are marked Guilty. Targets who fail take 4d6+12 magic damage. Targets who succeed take half damage.
Once per scene, spend a Fear to spotlight all other adversaries within Far range. Attacks they make while spotlighted in this way deal half damage.
A divine champion, head of a hallowed host of warriors who enforce their god’s will.
system.motives: Enforce dogma, fly, pronounce judgment, smite

system.description: The Kraken can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
While the Kraken has 7 or fewer marked HP, they can make their standard attack against two targets within range.

Make an attack roll against a target within Close range. On a success, mark a Stress to grab them with a tentacle and drag them beneath the water. The target is Restrained and Vulnerable until they break free with a successful Strength Roll or the Kraken takes Major or greater damage. While Restrained and Vulnerable in this way, a target must mark a Stress when they make an action roll.

Spend a Fear to spew a line of boiling water at any number of targets in a line up to Far range. All targets must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 4d6+9 physical damage. If a target marks an Armor Slot to reduce the damage, they must also mark a Stress.
When the Kraken makes a successful attack against a PC, you gain a Fear.
A legendary beast of the sea, bigger than the largest galleon, with sucker-laden tentacles and a terrifying maw.
system.motives: Consume, crush, drown, grapple

system.description: When the Oracle makes a successful attack, all PCs within Far range lose a Hope and you gain a Fear.
When a creature rolls a failure while within Very Far range of the Oracle, they must mark a Stress.

Spend a Fear to present a target within Far range with a vision of their personal nightmare. The target must make a Knowledge Reaction Roll. On a failure, they lose all Hope and take 2d20+4 direct magic damage. On a success, they take half damage and lose a Hope.
Once per day, spend 2 Fear to summon 2d4 Tier 2 or below Minions relevant to one of the PC’s personal nightmares. They appear at Close range relative to that PC.
When the Oracle sees a mortal creature, they instantly know one of their personal nightmares.
When the Oracle marks HP from an attack within Very Close range, you can mark a Stress to knock the attacker back to Far range and deal 2d10+4 physical damage.
A towering immortal and incarnation of fate, cursed to only see bad outcomes.
system.motives: Change environment, condemn, dishearten, toss aside

system.description: When the Abomination attacks, roll 2d4 and use the result as their attack modifier.
When a target takes damage from the Abomination, they must make an Instinct Reaction Roll. On a failure, they gain disadvantage on their next action roll and you gain a Fear.

Spend a Fear to rattle the edges of reality within Far range of the Abomination. All targets within that area must succeed on a Knowledge Reaction Roll or become Unstuck from reality until the end of the scene. When an Unstuck target spends Hope or marks Armor Slots, HP, or Stress, they must double the amount spent or marked.
When the Abomination takes damage, reduce it by 1d20. If the Abomination marks 1 or fewer Hit Points from a successful attack against them, you gain a Fear.
A chaotic mockery of life, constantly in flux.
system.motives: Demolish, devour, undermine

system.description: When a PC takes damage from the Corrupter, they lose a Hope.
Mark a Stress to spew partially digested portions of consumed realities at all targets within Close range. Targets must succeed on a Knowledge Reaction Roll or mark 2 Stress.
A shifting, formless mass seemingly made of chromatic light.
system.motives: Confuse, distract, overwhelm

system.description: The Thrall is defeated when they take any damage. For every 13 damage a PC deals to the Thrall, defeat an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Outer Realm Thralls within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 11 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
A vaguely humanoid form stripped of memory and identity.
system.motives: Destroy, disgust, disorient, intimidate

system.description: The Obsidian Predator can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
While flying, the Obsidian Predator gains a +3 bonus to their Difficulty.
The Obsidian Predator is resistant to physical damage.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against all targets within Close range. Targets the Obsidian Predator succeeds against take 4d6+4 physical damage and are knocked back to Far range and Vulnerable until their next roll with Hope.

If the Obsidian Predator is flying, mark a Stress to choose a point within Far range. Move to that point and make an attack against all targets within Very Close range. Targets the Obsidian Predator succeeds against take 2d10+6 physical damage and must mark a Stress and lose a Hope.
When the Obsidian Predator marks their last HP, replace them with the Molten Scourge and immediately spotlight them. VOLCANIC DRAGON: obsidian predator
A massive winged creature with obsidian scales and impossibly sharp claws.
system.motives: Defend lair, dive-bomb, fly, hunt, intimidate

system.description: The Molten Scourge can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
When the Molten Scourge takes damage, roll a number of d6s equal to HP marked. For each result of 4 or higher, you gain a Fear.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Very Close range. On a success, the target takes 4d8+1 physical damage, loses a Hope, and is knocked back to Close range. The Molten Scourge clears a Stress.

Spend a Fear to erupt lava from beneath the Molten Scourge’s scales, filling the area within Very Close range with molten lava. All targets in that area must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 4d6+6 physical damage and be knocked back to Close range. This area remains lava. When a creature other than the Molten Scourge enters that area or acts while inside of it, they must mark 6 HP.

When the Molten Scourge takes Major damage, roll a d10. On a result of 8 or higher, the Molten Scourge breathes a flow of lava in front of them within Far range. All targets in that area must make an Agility Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 2d10+4 physical damage, mark 1d4 Stress, and are Vulnerable until they clear a Stress. Targets who succeed take half damage and must mark a Stress.
When the Molten Scourge takes Severe damage from an attack within Very Close range, molten blood gushes from the wound and deals 2d10+4 direct physical damage to the attacker.

When the Molten Scourge marks their last HP, replace them with the Ashen Tyrant and immediately spotlight them.

VOLCANIC DRAGON: molten scourge
Enraged by their wounds, the dragon bursts into molten lava.
system.motives: Douse with lava, incinerate, repel Invaders, reposition

system.description: The Ashen Tyrant can be spotlighted up to four times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
Mark a Stress instead of spending a Fear to spotlight the Ashen Tyrant.
While flying, the Ashen Tyrant gains a +1 bonus to their Difficulty.
When a PC rolls a failure while within Close range of the Ashen Tyrant, they lose a Hope and you gain a Fear. If the PC can’t lose a Hope, they must mark a HP.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against all targets within Close range. Targets the Ashen Tyrant succeeds against take 2d20+2 physical damage, are knocked back to Close range of where they were, and must mark a Stress.

Spend a Fear to smash the ground and kick up ash within Far range. While within the ash cloud, a target has disadvantage on action rolls. The ash cloud clears the next time an adversary is spotlighted.

Countdown (1d12). Spend a Fear to activate. It ticks down when a PC rolls with Fear. When it triggers, the Ashen Tyrant thrashes about, causing environmental damage (such as an earthquake, avalanche, or collapsing walls). All targets within Far range must make a Strength Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 2d10+10 physical damage and are Restrained by the rubble until they break free with a successful Strength Roll. Targets who succeed take half damage. If the Ashen Tyrant is defeated while this countdown is active, trigger the countdown immediately as the destruction caused by their death throes.
No enemy has ever had the insolence to wound the dragon so. As the lava settles, it’s ground to ash like the dragon’s past foes.
system.motives: Choke, fly, intimidate, kill or be killed

system.description: When the Zombie makes a successful attack, all PCs within Far range lose a Hope and you gain a Fear.
PCs can’t spend Hope to use features against the Zombie.
Mark a Stress to make a standard attack against all targets within Very Close range. Targets the Zombie succeeds against are Vulnerable until their next rest.
When another adversary deals damage to a target within Very Close range of the Zombie, you can spend a Fear to add the Zombie’s standard attack damage to the damage roll.
A towering, muscular zombie with magically infused strength and skill.
system.motives: Consume, hound, maim, terrify

system.description: When the Legion has marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals 2d6+5 physical damage instead.
The Legion has resistance to physical damage.
The Legion can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.

When the Legion takes Minor damage from an attack within Melee range, you can mark a Stress to make a standard attack with advantage against the attacker.

VOLCANIC DRAGON: ashen tyrant
A large pack of undead, still powerful despite their rotting flesh.
system.motives: Consume brain, shred flesh, surround

system.description: When the Ahuizotl attacks from the water, it has advantage on the attack and deals an extra 1d6 damage.
Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Very Close range. On a success, deal 1d8+2 physical damage.

Spend a Fear to have the Ahuizotl grab a target within Close range with its tail, pull the target into Melee range, and temporarily Restrain them. The Ahuizotl has advantage on attacks against targets Restrained in this way.
A doglike ambush predator that has a clawed hand on the end of a long prehensile tail and drags victims into rivers to drown them.
system.motives: Ambush, drown, restrain

system.description: While the Atototl is flying, attacks against it is made with disadvantage.

Inside the Atototl is a stone that foretells good or ill fortune, depending on its color. A PC who searches the Atototl’s remains finds the stone and makes a fate roll. On an even result, the PC gains Hope equal to half the result, which they can distribute among the PCs however they wish. On an odd result, you gain Fear equal to half the result.

When a creature beyond Very Close range would deal damage to the Atototl with a weapon attack, you can spend a Fear to make an attack roll against them. On a success, whirling winds reflect the attack and deal the attacker’s damage back to them.
A majestic green water bird that has a ten-foot wingspan and is hunted for the fortune-telling stone inside their stomach.
system.motives: Avoid, escape, misdirect

system.description: If the Bugboar makes its first attack in a scene before it’s marked HP or Stress, it has advantage on the attack and deals an extra 1d8 damage.
When the Bugboar makes a successful standard attack, you can mark a Stress to deal an extra 1d6 damage.
When a condition would be imposed on the Bugboar, you can spend a Fear to negate it.
A large bipedal creature that has a tusked snout and coarse fur.
system.motives: Ambush, bully, seek carnage and shiny things

system.description: Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Ruffians within Close range of them. The Ruffians move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 1d8 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
When the Ruffian marks half their HP, roll a d6. On a result of 4 or higher, the Ruffian flees the scene. Otherwise, you gain a Fear.
A local laborer or artisan pushed by circumstances to assail others.
system.motives: Do violence, seek security and survival

system.description: The Crawler is defeated when it takes any damage. For every 3 damage a PC deals to the Crawler, the PC defeats an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.
Spend a Fear to force all PCs within Melee range of the Crawler to mark a Stress.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Darkweave Crawlers within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 2 physical damage each. Combine this damage.

When the Crawler makes a successful attack, you can mark a Stress to Exhaust the target until they succeed on a Strength Roll (9). While Exhausted, the target must mark a Stress each time they make an action roll.
A spider the size of a human head, woven out of shadow-silk.
system.motives: Hide in shadow, strike the unwary, wait for an opening

system.description: The Queen can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight her.
Once per scene, spend 2 Fear to summon up to two Darkweave adversaries (other than Darkweave Queens), who appear within Close range and immediately take the spotlight.
Spend a Fear to move up to Far range and make a standard attack with advantage.
When the Queen succeeds on a standard attack, you can spend a Fear to make the target Vulnerable and Restrained until they succeed on a Strength Roll (12) or take a rest.
When a PC fails an attack roll against the Queen, you gain a Fear.
A wagon-sized spider woven from shadow-silk by a long-forgotten god. Each of her many eyes bears the face of a different victim.
system.motives: Ambush prey, climb the walls and ceiling, misdirect, paralyze, stash bodies away for later, steal faces

system.description: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, the target is Vulnerable and Restrained until they succeed on a Strength Roll (10).

When the Spinner makes a successful attack against a target within Melee range, you can spend a Fear to make the target Shaky until they succeed on an Instinct Roll (10). While Shaky, the target has disadvantage on attack rolls.
A boar-sized arachnid woven from primordial shadow-silk.
system.motives: Bite, stick to the darkness

system.description: When the Swarmlings have marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals 1d4 physical damage instead. “Get ’em Off, Get ’em Off!” - Reaction: When an attack from the Swarmlings causes a target to mark HP, you can mark a Stress to make the target temporarily Covered in Spiders. While Covered in Spiders, the target must roll a d6 when they make an action roll. On a result of 4 or higher, they must mark a Stress or you gain a Fear.
A teeming swarm of tiny spiders woven out of shadow-silk.
system.motives: Burst out of holes, climb up legs, crawl into ears, scuttle under clothes

system.description: When the Elk moves from Close range or farther before making a standard attack, it deals 1d12+2 physical damage instead of its standard damage.
When the Elk marks a HP or Stress, it must succeed on a Reaction Roll (10) or flee the scene.
A large deer.
system.motives: Bound away, graze, rut, sense danger

system.description: While flying, the Falcon gains a +3 bonus to its Difficulty.
Mark a Stress to make a standard attack against a target from above. The Falcon gains a +2 bonus to the attack and damage rolls.
A bird of prey that has long, pointed wings and a notched beak.
system.motives: Circle, clutch, dive, spy

system.description: When the Warband has marked half or more of its HP, its standard attack deals 1d4+1 physical damage instead.
When the Warband marks its last Stress or an allied Leader is defeated, roll a d6. On a result of 2 or lower, the Warband flees the scene.
A cluster of small, strange creatures wearing armor fashioned from trash and stolen housewares.
system.motives: Ambush, celebrate a little too early, hit and run, infight, sabotage, sow chaos

system.description: The Harpy emits a foul stench that renders all non-Harpies Vulnerable while within Very Close range.
Mark a Stress to have the Harpy move in a straight line to a point within Far range and make an attack against a target in the Harpy’s path. On a success, the Harpy deals 3d6 physical damage.
A fierce and foul-smelling bird with an eight-foot wingspan and the upper body and face of a human.
system.motives: Defend nest, drop enemies from a great height, maraud from the air, screech incessantly

system.description: A PC must mark a Stress to move out of the Kelpie’s Melee range.
After the Kelpie interacts with or watches a creature for at least a hundred heartbeats, the Kelpie knows the physical form that creature would find most pleasing or alluring.

Mark a Stress to change the Kelpie’s physical form into any creature or object smaller than a wagon. A creature has disadvantage on rolls against the Kelpie while the Kelpie is in a form the creature finds pleasing or alluring.

Spend a Fear to have the Kelpie beguile a PC within Close range. The PC must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or become Enchanted until they take damage. While Enchanted, the PC perceives the Kelpie as a trusted friend or ally and will do what the Kelpie says unless it contradicts the PC’s most deeply held morals.
A river-dwelling shapeshifter who prefers an enchanting equine form in and out of the water.
system.motives: Adopt an attractive or useful shape, drown and devour, entice unwary travelers

system.description: The Masque Muerte can’t be Restrained.

Mark a Stress to make an attack against a PC within Close range. On a success, the target must mark a Stress and is temporarily Vulnerable as the Masque Muerte assaults them with a string of insulting taunts.
Spend a Fear to have the Masque Muerte suplex a Restrained PC, dealing 1d10+6 magic damage to them.
Spend a Fear to have the Masque Muerte momentarily remove their mask, revealing their horrifying face underneath. Each PC within Close range must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or mark a Stress.

When the Masque Muerte deals damage to a PC, you can spend a Fear to have a spectral wrestler appear and Pin the target until they escape with a successful Strength Roll. While Pinned, the target is Restrained and takes an extra 1d12 magic damage from the Masque Muerte’s attacks.
The raging soul of a villainous masked wrestler.
system.motives: Call out, embarrass, energize the audience, pin opponents to the ground

system.description: The Mechanorb gains a +1 bonus to their Difficulty for each other Mechanorb within Close range.

Pool. When the Mechanorb fails an attack roll, add a token to the Mechanorb Pool. All Mechanorbs in the scene gain a bonus to attack rolls equal to the number of tokens in the Mechanorb Pool. Clear all tokens when any Mechanorb takes Severe damage or is defeated.
A floating clockwork sphere that has telescoping limbs and comes from a realm of machines and metal.
system.motives: Coordinate, (dis)assemble, move orthogonally, speak in binary

system.description: The Troll can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.

Countdown. When combat begins, activate a countdown with a value equal to the number of PCs. When the Troll takes damage, reduce the severity by one threshold, then tick down the countdown. When it triggers, the Troll evolves (see “Enraged Mountain Troll”).
Mark a Stress to make an attack against all targets in front of the Troll within Very Close range. Targets the Troll succeeds against take 2d8+2 physical damage.

The Troll loses their “Stolen Armor” and “Flail Swipe” features, then gains a +1 bonus to their Difficulty. Additionally, they gain the “Double Swipe” feature and replace “Skull Flail” with the following standard attack: Claw Swipe: Very Close | 1d10+3 phy Double Swipe - Action: Spend a Fear to move up to Close range and make two standard attacks against a target within Melee range. If both attacks succeed, combine the damage, and the target loses a Hope.
A hideous giant born out of a massive rock. They wear purloined armor and a belt of severed heads or skulls.
system.motives: Ambush, bellow, hurl large boulders, smash, stomp

system.description: Make an attack roll against a target within Close range. On a success, the target becomes Restrained and Vulnerable until they escape with a successful Strength Roll.

Mark a Stress to have the Octopus squirt ink. On land, the ink covers the ground within Very Close range. Each creature who moves through that area must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or slip and fall, becoming Vulnerable until they exit the area. If this feature is used while the Octopus is underwater, it instead creates a cloud of darkness that fills an area within Very Close range and blocks line of sight.
An aquatic, soft-bodied mollusk that has eight sucker-bearing arms and a hard, beaklike jaw.
system.motives: Crawl along the ocean floor, eat fish, squirt ink to escape

system.description: While Hidden, the Panther gains a +2 bonus to its attack rolls.
Mark a Stress to have the Panther leap into Melee range of a target within Far range and make an attack against them. On a success, deal 1d12+2 physical damage.
A large feline predator that stalks its prey from the shadows.
system.motives: Climb trees, pounce, stalk

system.description: The Poltergeist has resistance to physical damage. Mark a Stress to move up to Close range through solid objects.

Mark a Stress to have the Poltergeist inhabit a nonmagical object that is entirely within Close range, infusing the object with a ghostly glow. The next time the Poltergeist would take damage, the object is destroyed instead, and the Poltergeist is expelled from it.

Spend a Fear to have the Poltergeist pull all unequipped nonmagical objects within Very Close range into a violent vortex. Each target in that area must make an Agility Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 1d12+2 physical damage. Targets who succeed take half damage.
A baleful, translucent spirit that possesses inanimate objects.
system.motives: Flicker candles, rattle chains, shake windows, throw people around the room

system.description: The Phantom has resistance to physical damage and can move through solid objects.
A PC who takes the spotlight within Very Close range of the Phantom must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll (10) or mark a Stress.

Countdown (1d6). When the Phantom is defeated, you can spend a Fear to activate the countdown. It ticks down when a PC rolls with Fear. When it triggers, clear the Phantom’s HP and immediately spotlight them.
The echo of a lost soul in the form of an ectoplasmic shadow.
system.motives: Create cold spots, swoop through the air, whisper dark tidings

system.description: When the Rabble Mawb has marked half or more of its HP, its standard attack deals 1d4+1 physical damage instead.

When the Rabble Mawb is defeated, you can spend a Fear to bring it back to life, clearing all HP and Stress. The Rabble Mawb gains a bonus to all rolls equal to the number of times this feature has been used by this Rabble Mawb.
These cat-sized balls of hair, limbs, and teeth travel in a “mawb” of a dozen.
system.motives: Chitter and chew, clump together, roll around

system.description: When the Biters have marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals 1d4+2 physical damage instead.
A PC must mark a Stress to move out of the Biters’ Melee range.
A troop of fist-sized fey creatures who have needle-sharp teeth and conical red caps sealed on their heads with candle wax.
system.motives: Bring ’em down, celebrate tiny victories, giggle and chitter, scamper between the walls

system.description: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 3d4+10 physical damage. A target who marks HP from this attack is Restrained until they clear a HP.
When the Breaker makes a successful standard attack, you can spend a Fear to make the target temporarily Vulnerable.
A large, brutish fey creature who has a conical red cap sealed on their head with candle wax.
system.motives: Beat chest and bellow, ragdoll puny enemies, rush forward recklessly

system.description: Mark a Stress to make a standard attack against up to three targets. For each target who marks HP, you gain a Fear.
Mark a Stress to make a standard attack against a target within Far range. If the Butcher is Hidden, they make the attack with advantage.
A halfling-sized fey creature who hacks their victims apart with a variety of cutting implements. They wear a conical red hat sealed on their head with candle wax.
system.motives: Grin disconcertingly, hack and slash, scramble

system.description: When the Candlemaker appears, place 5 tokens on this stat block. Remove a token whenever the Candlemaker marks a HP. While this stat block has 1 or more tokens on it, the Candlemaker is Hidden.

The light of the Candlemaker’s Hand of Glory inspires bloodlust in their allies. While this stat block has 1 or more tokens on it, each Redcap adversary within Close range gains a +1 bonus to their damage rolls.

Spend a token from this stat block. The Candlemaker conjures a ball of fire on a group of PCs within Far range. Each target must make an Agility Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 2d10 magic damage. Targets who succeed take half damage.
A pale, gaunt cult leader wearing a conical red cap sealed on their head with candle wax. They wield a long rod with a candle atop it made from a hanged criminal’s hand.
system.motives: Cast long shadows, keep out of the fray, show them the light

system.description: The Skinner is defeated when they take any damage. For every 4 damage a PC deals to the Skinner, the PC defeats an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.
When a PC fails a roll, they take 1 physical damage for each Skinner within Melee range of them. Combine this damage.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Redcap Skinners within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 2 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
A cat-sized fey creature wielding a straight razor and wearing a conical red cap sealed on their head with candle wax.
system.motives: Flense, giggle, scrape, slice

system.description: The Rugaru can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.
While in moonlight, the Rugaru gains a +2 bonus to their Difficulty.

When a PC marks HP from the Rugaru’s standard attack, add a token to this stat block. The Rugaru gains a bonus to attack rolls equal to the number of tokens on this stat block. Clear all tokens when the Rugaru takes Severe damage.

Mark a Stress to force each PC within Far range to make a Presence Reaction Roll (15). Targets who fail lose a Hope. Gain a Fear for each Hope lost. If a PC has no Hope, they must mark a Stress and become Vulnerable until they roll with Hope.
Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d12+2 direct physical damage.
A wolf-headed humanoid cursed by the gods to prowl the swamps in search of blood.
system.motives: Blaspheme, go for the throat, stalk, terrorize

system.description: Mark a Stress to attack a target within Melee range. On a success, the target takes 1d12 physical damage and must mark an Armor Slot without gaining its benefit (they can still use armor to reduce the damage).

When a creature marks HP, you can spend a Fear to spotlight all Sawtoothed Gillbeasts within Very Close range of them. Those Gillbeasts move into Melee range of the creature and each make a standard attack against them. If any attacks succeed, combine their damage.
When the Gillbeast would mark any number of HP, roll a d6. On a result of 6, you can mark a Stress instead.
A stocky fish creature that has rows of razor-sharp teeth.
system.motives: Clamber ashore, hit and run, peek above the waterline

system.description: The Mage can be spotlighted up to three times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.

Mark a Stress to roll a d6. The Mage uses the corresponding move: 1–2: Dimension Rift. Choose a target within Far range. The target teleports to a point you choose within Close range of their original position and takes 2d6 direct magic damage as their body and mind reassemble. 3–4: Time Dilation. Choose a group of PCs within Far range. Each target is Slowed until they roll with Hope. While Slowed, a target is Vulnerable and must mark a Stress when they move. 5–6: Discordant Visions. Make an attack against up to three targets within Close range. Targets the Mage succeeds against take 2d8 direct magic damage.
When the Mage marks HP, roll a number of d6s equal to the number of Stress the Mage has marked. The Mage deals direct magic damage equal to the total result to all PCs within Very Close range.
A spellcaster with a psyche broken by knowledge best left hidden.
system.motives: Babble in an unknown language, laugh unsettlingly, wield power beyond control

system.description: The Armor can’t be forced to mark Stress. When an effect would cause it to mark Stress, the Armor ignores that part of the effect.
Once per scene when the Armor is defeated, you can spend a Fear to reactivate it. Clear 2 HP and immediately spotlight it.
An empty suit of full plate armor that glows with a faint corona of ghostly light.
system.motives: Clank noisily, move like clockwork, watch silently

system.description: The Viper is defeated when it takes any damage. For every 4 damage a PC deals to the Viper, the PC defeats an additional Minion within range the attack would succeed against.
When the Viper makes a successful standard attack, the target becomes temporarily Envenomated. While Envenomated, the target must mark a Stress whenever they make an action roll.

Spend a Fear to choose a target and spotlight all Vipers within Close range of them. Those Minions move into Melee range of the target and make one shared attack roll. On a success, they deal 1 physical damage each. Combine this damage.
A small serpent that envenomates its prey with hinged fangs.
system.motives: Lie in wait, slither, strike

system.description: The Creation can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight it.
The Creation doesn’t take extra damage from attacks that critically succeed against it.

Mark a Stress to have the Creation throw a ball of wax at a target within Far range. Make an attack against the target. On a success, the target takes 1d12+2 physical damage and becomes Restrained until they succeed on a Strength Roll (15).

When a PC within Melee range of the Creation makes a weapon attack against it, roll a d6. On a 5 or higher, the attacker’s weapon gets stuck in the Creation and can be removed only with a successful Strength Roll (15).

When the Creation makes a successful standard attack against a target within Melee range, you can spend a Fear to Trap the target inside the Creation’s wax body. While Trapped, the target is Restrained and must mark a Stress and move with the Creation each time it’s spotlighted. A Trapped creature is freed when the Creation takes Major or greater damage.
A ten-foot-tall, semisolid (and semisentient) candle wax construct.
system.motives: Lumber menacingly, moan with the pain of unlife, smother

system.description: When the Will-o’-the-Wisps have marked half or more of their HP, their standard attack deals 1d4−1 magic damage instead.
The Will-o’-the-Wisps pulse and dance in hypnotic, color-changing patterns that entrance any creature who looks upon them. All targets within Very Close range of the Will-o’-the-Wisps are Vulnerable.

Spend a Fear to have the Will-o’-the-Wisps trace looping light trails through the air, leaving afterimages that beg to be deciphered. Each PC within Far range must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll (13) or mark a Stress and move up to Close range toward the Will-o’-the-Wisps.
Lazily floating orbs of color-shifting werelight.
system.motives: Dazzle and distract, disorient, lead astray

system.description: The Yufo can mentally communicate with creatures within Very Far range.
The Yufo is immune to abilities and features that would affect or alter its thoughts or emotions.

Spend a Fear and choose up to three targets within Close range. Each target must succeed on a Instinct Reaction Roll or become desynced from reality and have disadvantage on Instinct Rolls until they use a downtime move to ground their psyches in the now.

When the Yufo succeeds on a standard attack, you can mark a Stress to have the Yufo excrete an entropic acid through its skin, giving the target a −2 penalty to their damage thresholds until they use a downtime move to repair their armor.
A large, interdimensional jellyfishlike creature that floats in and out of the timestream.
system.motives: Exchange information about possible timelines, feed on heightened emotions, watch from the shadows

system.description: The Banshee has resistance to physical damage. Mark a Stress to move up to Close range through solid objects.
When the Banshee makes a successful attack, all PCs within Close range lose a Hope, and you gain a Fear.

Up to three times per scene, spend a Fear to have the Banshee teleport up to Very Far range and scare a PC within Melee range. The PC marks 1d4 Stress. If this causes them to mark HP, they also lose a Hope.
